issue:generate.description: Generate ticket descriptions from local files, repo-scoped artifacts via --repos, URLs, or Jira keys. Local .md, .json, .yaml, and .yml files that parse as tickets are imported as tickets; files that are not recognized as ticket-formatted content remain plain file sources. When --repos points to a local checkout, wf bootstraps config from that repo and accepts either module.exports or export default in wf.config.js, including ESM repos. Generated output normalizes em dashes to ASCII " - " before display or save. Can use an agent backend when stages.generate.agent: true is configured

issue:implement.description: Carry out an implementation plan from a ticket-backed, hashed, or custom plan artifact. Delegates the generate-and-verify loop to the Anthropic or OpenAI agent backend based on stages.implement.provider. Progress events are streamed to the terminal so you can follow task and tool activity while edits are being generated. Both backends emit stable SDK task and tool progress lines plus explicit file mutation logs and verification logs so terminal output stays human-readable while the agent works. Verification commands are expected to be repo-root-relative; stale plan artifacts that still embed redundant repo-selection `cd` prefixes are normalized, while cross-repo directory jumps are treated as setup errors. Set stages.implement.provider to anthropic or openai in wf.config to select the backend. The Anthropic backend explicitly loads ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the repository-root CLAUDE.md, warning when either file is missing. The OpenAI backend loads ~/.openai/OPENAI.md and the repository-root .openai/OPENAI.md with the same warning behavior and only exposes an exact-match verify_command tool for whitelisted verification commands. When running from source, use `yarn start issue:implement ...` for the implementation stage and `yarn start issue:commit -c` to stage the final conventional commit once the work is accepted. Unsupported providers (google, deepseek) fail fast with a clear error listing supported providers. Run issue:fetch then issue:plan before calling this command for ticket-backed workflows. When a hashed plan artifact is provided, the action is inferred from the filename/manifest and `--action` becomes optional, but any supplied action is still validated against the resolved artifact. Examples: wf issue:implement PROJ-123 | wf issue:implement 2026-05-04-1a2b3c4d-fix-plan.json | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --repos my-repo | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --repos repo-a repo-b | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --dry-run
